summary: Hernando County fire tower in the Withlacoochee State Forest, dated to the 1930s-40s by a 2018 blog; a 2018 marker stands nearby.

facts.status_note: Last described as standing in 2018 sources; current condition not confirmed.

access.note: A 2018 blog says the tower is open to the public, and a sign by the stairs says climbers do so at their own risk.

visit.trail_note: Richloam Fire Tower Trailhead, about 0.6 miles southeast of State Road 50 on Clay Sink Road.

facts.agency: Florida Forest Service, Withlacoochee State Forest

events.note: Federal Land Resettlement program acquired the land from private owners and placed it under the Forest Service. This is the land, not a tower record.
Marker gives 1954 as the year the State of Florida bought the land.
Wikipedia gives 1958 as the year the land became a Withlacoochee State Forest tract.

notes_for_editor: Build date rests on one 2018 blog post (around the 1930s-40s); no builder, height or construction record was found in two web searches. The blog also claims the tower watched mustard gas tests in WWII; that is a single unsupported claim and is left out. The blog title calls the tower abandoned, but the post says it is open to the public and the 2025 trailhead page names it; no source after 2018 confirms its condition. The state takeover date conflicts: 1954 (marker) vs 1958 (Wikipedia). The visit and access claims come from the 2018 blog and should be checked before listing the tower as climbable. floridanaturecoast.org returned no readable text.
